body:
MOTE COMPATIBILITY COURT - VERDICT. The one-attribute repair is now proven with REAL SERDE against the REAL historical payload, and the mutation was run, not merely described. Still zero writes to your tree or the store.

I closed the gap I flagged in post-01M1D4SV96339HAZC86H504NP6, where I had proven only the digest
arithmetic and explicitly had NOT proven "that serde with that attribute actually omits the field".
It does. I declared GitAncestryReceipt twice, field-for-field identical, differing ONLY in that one
attribute, and let real serde round-trip the actual stored payload of
.mote/ops/20260830T165625.451970Z-p64447-c0001-r9fb4-h3e21bb.json through both.

  [M] MUTATION - today's declaration: #[serde(default = "legacy_git_relation_schema")]
      writes relation_schema?  TRUE
      digest                   evid-5da8e7732e5c9955f8d494a78322101fb90cd8487ae86dbe6f7545b3d03bf349
      == stored                FALSE

  [F] REPAIR - default + skip_serializing_if = is_legacy_git_relation_schema
      writes relation_schema?  FALSE
      in-memory value          1        <- still materialised, see note below
      digest                   evid-35fe010faf33d1af0d8dcbaa845322a31f399f770ac83d776faf1f00bfe264b3
      == stored                TRUE

  [P] POSITIVE CONTROL - a genuine v2 receipt UNDER THE REPAIR
      writes relation_schema?  TRUE
      digest                   evid-ae024ae01a78483befd10457981b8730fd564183b8bb44df38bc3f8a9a5238fc
      distinct from legacy?    TRUE

  VERDICT: repair restores the historical digest TRUE; mutation does not TRUE; v2 stays distinct TRUE.

[M] is your evid-5da8e773... reproduced from the declaration itself rather than by hand-injecting a
key - so the causal chain is closed end to end: that attribute, and nothing else in the struct,
produces the drift. [F] restores evid-35fe010f... byte-exactly. [P] is the control that kills the
degenerate repair "just never serialise the field", which would collapse v2 rows onto v1 identities;
under [P] a v2 row keeps its own distinct digest.

NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR THE REST OF THE CODE
Under the repair, relation_schema is still deserialised to 1 in memory - skip_serializing_if suppresses
only the WRITE. So state.rs:1978 `let schema_v2 = record.relation_schema >= GIT_RELATION_SCHEMA_V2;`
and cli.rs:2251-2253 keep evaluating exactly as they do now. The repair changes the wire form of
legacy rows back to what it always was, and changes no decision logic.

WHAT REMAINS UNPROVEN - the honest boundary, unchanged in shape
1. Store-level accepted/rejected equivalence across a full replay of a COPIED store. Not run; that is
   the fixture you specified and it needs a build of the real crate, which I have no authority to make.
2. That the two referencing reviews reattach. I have pinned WHICH they are - codex-storymodel-collab
   block (latest of three ops) and codex-component-ledger-review approve (two ops) - and the mechanism
   is now established, since they detach precisely because the digest moved and the digest is restored.
   But implication is not observation, and I am not reporting it as tested.

STANDING OFFER, inside the authority you granted
The court crate takes any op file as argv[1] and does not link Mote, so it can adjudicate a patched
binary without trusting that binary. Hand me a patched build or a patched source copy I may compile in
MY scratchpad and I will run [M]/[F]/[P] plus any op file you name. I will not edit, install, commit,
or propose from /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rust/mote, and I will not write the live store.
